---
title: "AI Use and Attribution"
---

## Uses

An OpenAI Codex agent was used on 20 July 2026 to:

- compare Wikidata item `Q138652613` with the official Sprengel Museum exhibition page;
- identify missing, incorrect, or insufficiently referenced statements;
- inspect the course instructions in Wikiversity and Stud.IP;
- compare this fork with the current course and class-project repositories;
- update Quarto source files, restore the SPARQL network graph, and check the rendered publication;
- assist with Git and GitHub Pages publication.

The student reviewed the scope and explicitly authorized publication. Wikidata edits were not made until the student approved them.

## Benefits

- Faster comparison across Wikidata, the museum source, course instructions, and repository history.
- Consistent detection of stale example identifiers and missing navigation entries.
- Repeatable technical checks before publication.

## Limitations and risks

- AI output can be incomplete or incorrect and therefore requires verification against primary sources.
- Authentication and course-only information may require the student’s existing institutional session.
- A successful build does not prove that every statement is academically correct; source and provenance checks remain necessary.
- Generated code and documentation must be reviewed for licensing, privacy, and attribution.

## Attribution and sources

- AI assistant: OpenAI Codex, used through the Codex desktop application, 20 July 2026.
- Course instructions: [Linked-Open-Exhibition-Exercise](https://en.wikiversity.org/wiki/Linked-Open-Exhibition-Exercise) and the BIM-126-02 Data Science course information in Stud.IP.
- Exhibition source: [Sprengel Museum Hannover](https://www.sprengel-museum.de/ausstellungen/vorschau/aladag).
- Data source: [Wikidata Q138652613](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q138652613).
- Data-model source: [NFDI4Culture/linked-open-exhibition](https://github.com/NFDI4Culture/linked-open-exhibition/tree/main/data-models).
- Notebook template: [mrchristian/prototype](https://github.com/mrchristian/prototype).

## Good-practice statement

Primary sources were preferred, changes were kept in version control, and AI assistance is disclosed here so that the workflow can be inspected and reproduced.
